children: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell to 4.99% on Thursday, below the 2007 high of 5.04% reached earlier in the week.

The decline came after the Fed raised interest rates and Chair Warsh reaffirmed the central bank’s commitment to tackling inflation, reassuring investors about its policy credibility and determination to contain price pressures.
The central bank raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25bps, marking its first rate hike since July 2023, and signalled at least one further increase in borrowing costs this year.
While the move had been fully priced in ahead of the decision, investors had been concerned that a surprise decision to hold rates could trigger a surge in market volatility.

Meanwhile, the yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which is more sensitive to near-term Federal Reserve policy, edged down to 4.73%, while the yield on 30-year Treasury bonds, which are more sensitive to longer-term inflation and geopolitical risks, fell to 5.34%.

title: Treasury Yields Fall After Fed
